title: Why Do Concrete Bridges Crack?
subtitle: And why can't you just patch them with Elmer's glue?
eli5: Concrete expands in summer heat, freezes in winter, and gets hammered by 80,000-lb semi-trucks. Cracks form deep inside. If water gets in, it rusts the rebar and the bridge collapses.
analogy: Imagine a tooth cavity. You can't just smear toothpaste on top of the tooth and call it fixed. A dentist has to drill in, clean the root, and inject filling under pressure all the way to the bottom. Concrete crack repair is structural root canal surgery for highway overpasses.
why_jack_cares: Department of Transportation (DOT) engineers legally mandate high-pressure epoxy injection. It's not optional maintenance—contractors face massive penalties if they don't repair it.

interactive_quiz.question: Why do engineers inject liquid epoxy under 1,000+ PSI?
options: To make the concrete look shiny for cars
To force liquid glue through microscopic cracks all the way to the rebar
Because state inspectors love wasting money
interactive_quiz.explanation: Exactly! Hairline cracks run feet deep into concrete. Only high pressure can force viscous epoxy all the way to the core.

title: What On Earth Is An 'Injecti-Port'?
subtitle: The 10-Cent Plastic Tee That Prints Cash
eli5: You can't just stick a hose against concrete and pump glue—it will spray everywhere. A port is a small plastic tee that gets glued over the crack. The pump locks onto it to inject resin, and an internal check ball stops the glue from shooting back in your face.
analogy: It's like an IV port in an arm at a hospital. The doctor tapes the port to your vein so medicine can be pushed in cleanly without making a mess or leaking back out.
why_jack_cares: A single bridge deck or parking garage repair can use 5,000 to 20,000 ports. They are 100% disposable single-use plastic. Once the epoxy hardens, they are knocked off with a hammer and thrown in the trash.

interactive_quiz.question: What happens to the port after the epoxy cures?
options: It gets cleaned and reused on the next job
It is knocked off and thrown away—single use only
It melts into the concrete
interactive_quiz.explanation: Bingo! They are 100% disposable single-use items. Every project requires a brand new box of ports.
